title: Chronic pain
hookLine: long pain can be carried with others
tomorrow: what could possibly be missing from Christ's sufferings?

lines: A HOUSE TOO FULL TO ENTER.
cards: A grandmother who has folded tamales for years, wincing only when she thinks nobody's looking. Long pain gets quiet. You stop mentioning it because it never changes, and people stop asking.
Now, a house in Capernaum, so packed nobody can get through the door. Inside, Jesus is teaching. And above everyone's heads, the roof starts to come apart.
Dust falls. Daylight. Four men are up there, digging.

teach.b: Mark explains, in the Douay-Rheims: "And they came to him, bringing one sick of the palsy, who was carried by four." The man can't walk. The crowd won't move.
So his friends open the roof and lower his bed right down in front of Jesus.

teach.h: WHEN JESUS HAD SEEN THEIR FAITH.
teach.b: Then a small line with a big turn: "And when Jesus had seen their faith." One to tell a friend: it's their faith, the four friends', that Jesus sees first.
The man on the bed didn't have to carry his own hope down through the ceiling. Not every long pain in scripture lifts.

Paul writes of a sting in his flesh that he begged God to take away, and the answer he got was, "My grace is sufficient for thee: for power is made perfect in infirmity." The pain stayed. So did the grace.
That's why Catholics ask each other for prayers, put names on parish prayer lists, and have Masses offered for the sick.
Paul says it plainly to the Galatians: "Bear ye one another's burdens; and so you shall fulfil the law of Christ." Chronic pain may not be fixable.
It's still meant to be carried by more than one.

how: Catholics ask one another for prayers, add names to parish prayer lists, and have Masses offered for the sick; parish ministers may bring Communion to people who can't leave home.

o: pain that lasts a long time and doesn't go away
a punishment that lasts until you repent
a sudden injury that heals within a few days

games.q: the roof and the thorn — tap the pairs.
p: my grace is sufficient for thee

s: in Mark 2, Jesus sees the faith of the man's friends
and when Jesus had seen their faith: the four who carried him.
in scripture, if you pray hard enough every pain is taken away
Paul begged for his to go; the answer was grace that is sufficient, and the pain stayed.
asking others to pray for you is a sign of weak faith
bear ye one another's burdens: carrying together is how the law of Christ is fulfilled.

games.q: a teammate has had migraines for two years. she's stopped mentioning them, and stopped coming to team dinners. what do the four on the roof suggest?
o: ask what helps, and make the plan around her, not without her.
wait until she asks; bringing it up might embarrass her.
tell her about a cure you read about so she can finally fix it.
games.why: the four didn't fix the man; they carried him where help was. long pain gets quiet, so friends go first.

practice: Think of one person you trust. Send them a short message asking them to pray for you, or to keep you in mind, about one thing that's been heavy a long time.
You don't have to explain it all; the four on the roof never gave a speech. Then sit quietly while it goes.

wordCard.voice: Chronic pain. Pain that lasts and lasts, which this tradition says no one should have to carry alone. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: lasting a long time, from chronos, time. the English word chronic comes from it.

carryVoice: Your line: carried together, four friends and a hole in the roof. See you tomorrow.
